rv.q: Monstering the Rocketman is a highly entertaining and sharply observed cautionary tale.
Expanded a little from its festival roots, the show still bowls along, with lots of laughs to be found swimming in this sewer of amoralty.
For all of its fascination with the ethical lines reporters cross, in the end the text does little more than gesture vaguely at the problem.
Unfortunately, Naylor also believes himself an actor and has mistakenly chosen to perform the piece himself.
Naylor clearly puts his heart and soul into the piece.

However, it’s a sad, sad situation as this production squanders all of that with messy, uneven and frustrating writing that does a disservice to both the star it speaks of, and the clearly talented individuals working on this show.
Henry Naylor’s Monstering the Rocketman, which he also performs, dramatises the affair with precision and urgency.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this fast-paced one-man show about tabloid journalism and Elton John's libel case. While some praise its sharp wit and entertaining examination of press ethics, others find it falls short of its Edinburgh Fringe acclaim.
